filename: Understanding Perturbed Parameter Ensemble Sensitivities Using A Contrastive Learning Approach.pdf
title: Understanding Perturbed Parameter Ensemble Sensitivities Using A Contrastive Learning Approach
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
testbed_rationale: The datasets consist of monthly-mean, 2D top-of-atmosphere radiative fluxes and column liquid water paths designed for model evaluation and contrastive embedding analysis rather than high-frequency 3D process-level training for subgrid parameterizations.
pain_points: High-dimensional multivariate outputs of perturbed parameter ensembles make diagnosing parametric uncertainty and structural biases difficult.
Equifinality where multiple parameter configurations yield similar scalar error metrics despite structural errors.
Compensating regional or seasonal errors across cloud and radiation variables.
High computational cost of bin microphysics schemes requiring neural network emulation (TAU-ML).
extraction_notes: The preprint uses an existing neural network emulator (TAU-ML) inside one of the CAM6 PPEs, but the primary ML contribution of this work is an offline self-supervised contrastive learning architecture and Integrated Gradients XAI pipeline to analyze PPE parameter sensitivity and structural model errors.
